# Artifacts

Everything `scripts/run_full_pipeline.py` produces. Regenerate with:

```bash
python scripts/run_full_pipeline.py
```

## Read this first

**The corpus is synthetic.** It is generated by the physically-based water
balance in `smml.physics.simulator` — a layered tipping-bucket cascade with SCS
Curve Number runoff, FAO-56 evapotranspiration, irrigation scheduled by depletion
trigger, and a sensor response model that imposes clay and salinity bias — not
measured in any field.

The environment this was built in has no network access to any soil moisture data
host, so no real observation could be harvested. These results demonstrate that
the pipeline works end to end and that its diagnostics behave correctly. They say
**nothing** about accuracy on real soils, and a Saxton-Rawls baseline is
unusually strong here because the generator shares its pedotransfer assumptions.
Every figure carries that notice in the corner.

Once `smml verify endpoints` has been run on an open network and the connectors
fixed against it, the same script points at the harvested database by changing
one path.

## `database/`

The harmonized database, in three forms of the same content:

| Form | Use |
|---|---|
| `observations/`, `sites/`, `weather/`, `irrigation/` | Partitioned Parquet — the working store. Appendable, idempotent, partition-pruned. |
| `soil_moisture.duckdb` | One portable file. Open it anywhere; needs neither this package nor the directory tree. |
| `csv/` | Spreadsheet-readable. The observation table is capped; the full table is in the other two. |

```sql
-- in the duckdb file
SELECT texture_class, count(*) AS n, round(avg(theta_m3m3), 4) AS mean_theta
FROM observations o JOIN sites s USING (site_id)
WHERE quality_flag = 'G' AND depth_top_cm < 15
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC;
```

Note `theta_m3m3` and `theta_clay_corrected_m3m3` are separate columns. The
original observation is never overwritten — a correction computed from an
*estimated* clay content can be worse than none, and the only way to find out is
to be able to compare.

## `figures/`

| File | What it shows |
|---|---|
| `01_measured_vs_predicted.png` | The 1:1 scatter, faceted by depth, with the ±0.04 m³/m³ accuracy band |
| `02_time_series.png` | Measured and predicted through a season at held-out sites |
| `03_performance_by_depth.png` | RMSE, ubRMSE and bias down the profile |
| `04_error_by_stratum.png` | Error by texture, by salinity, and against clay content |
| `05_clay_correction_effect.png` | Bias against clay, before and after correcting the training target |
| `06_skill_decomposition.png` | Skill between sites against skill within a site |

Faceted by depth rather than coloured by it: six depths exceed the three-series
cap for forms where every pair is on screen at once, and depth is *ordered*, so a
facet grid preserves an ordering that six arbitrary hues would destroy.

## `results/`

| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `model_comparison.csv` | Every model and baseline on identical folds |
| `clay_correction_contrast.csv` | The same model fitted to the raw and the corrected target |
| `performance_by_depth.csv`, `performance_by_texture.csv` | Stratified metrics |
| `targets_product_A.csv`, `targets_product_B.csv` | Pass/fail against the success criteria |
| `best_hyperparameters.yaml`, `hyperparameter_importance.csv` | The Optuna search |
| `qc_summary.csv` | Quality control flag rates |
| `feature_importance.csv` | Top features by gain |
| `out_of_fold_predictions.parquet` | Every held-out prediction, for recomputing any metric |
| `run_summary.json` | The whole run in one file |

`out_of_fold_predictions.parquet` is the primary output, not the metrics. Having
every prediction the model made on data it did not see lets any metric be
recomputed later and errors sliced by any covariate.

## How the evaluation is set up

Leave-site-out cross-validation: whole sites are held out, so the model is scored
on fields it has never seen. That is the deployment question and it is much
harder than a random split — `smml evaluate --include-optimism` quantifies the
gap on your own data.

Scored against `theta_true_m3m3`, the simulator's true water content, while
trained on `theta_clay_corrected_m3m3`, the sensor reading after the
bound-water correction. That separation is what makes the clay-correction
contrast measurable at all, and it is only possible on synthetic data — with real
observations there is no true value to score against, which is why gravimetric
calibration samples matter so much.
